intent.note: Task clause: 'Decide per case whether the PRODUCT is wrong ... or the CASE compares a spelling it should normalise ... say which shells the printed command targets and quote for them ... never weaken a case to the observed output.' The diff keeps shlex.quote (executable bytes of audit-status.py unchanged) and states the target shell in `_shell_word`'s docstring (POSIX sh / Git for Windows' sh, not cmd.exe or PowerShell); `_proc_group.locate_sh` (_proc_group.py:302) exists and resolves that shell, so the stated basis holds. The decision is defensible: every other printed command in the plugin is POSIX-quoted and the inner `submodule foreach` command is read by git's own sh. A reader could still argue a Windows user pasting into PowerShell/cmd is not served; the docstring now says so openly rather than hiding it. On the weakening question: no case was loosened to the observed output. kt5/kt9 went from a substring/startswith test to an exact shell word list (stricter); kt7 went from exact-text counts to word-based plus `len(saves)==2`; kt9b is `[:5] == [git, worktree, remove, other, '-']`, the same prefix, read as words; kt6b now runs the row's printed text as written instead of rebuilding argv by `split(' ')`, and adds a before-listing so 'git lists it no more' is a watched change (the old `('worktree %s' % tree) not in listed` was a spelling that could never match); kt8 selects saves by the `-C` word a shell reads and runs them under the plugin's resolved shell, also keeping `len(saves)==2`. Claim vs diff: the outcome describes the diff accurately (docstring-only product change, helpers _posix_words/_remedy_after/_run_as_written/_listed_worktrees/_one_spelling all present). Its reading of kt6b (quoting, not a real/via mismatch) is consistent with the diff (the case already realpaths its base). Not verified by me: the Windows legs, the spaced and cp1252 runs, and the mutation proofs; the executor says Windows was not measured, and kt6b/kt8 now execute git worktree remove/update-ref/submodule-foreach under git's sh there for the first time.
